list_note: The two published lists are cohorts of locations and not treatment types. The 2025 list holds signage, e-scooter corrals, bicycle corrals, street improvement projects, turn calming outside a street improvement project, bikeshare and a direction change. The 2024 list publishes no type at all, so the class shown for a 2024 record is recovered from the inventory at the same corner, and that recovery reproduces turn calming exactly and signage only on 80.6 per cent when tested against the 2025 list, where the type is published.

hydrants.name: Hydrants
hydrants.publisher: NYC Open Data (City of New York), Department of Environmental Protection
hydrants.access: Socrata SODA 2.0 REST API, no app token, retries with backoff
hydrants.coverage: a current snapshot with no history; 109,725 hydrants carry a position
hydrants.licence: No per dataset licence stated; NYC Open Data Terms of Use apply
hydrants.roles: covariate: curb already cleared before the programme, used for a pre-registered subgroup split and for a balance check between arms
hydrants.notes: New York State Vehicle and Traffic Law section 1202 prohibits parking within 15 feet of a hydrant, being 4.572 m, so a corner carrying one already had cleared curb before the daylighting programme reached it. The record carries no installation date, so it cannot be used as a treatment with an event time and is used only as a characteristic of a corner, held fixed over the study period.

busstops.name: MTA Current Bus Stops
busstops.publisher: NY Open Data (State of New York), Metropolitan Transportation Authority
busstops.access: Socrata SODA 2.0 REST API, no app token, retries with backoff
busstops.coverage: the network currently in effect, with no history
busstops.licence: No per dataset licence stated; data.ny.gov Terms of Use apply
busstops.roles: covariate: curb already cleared before the programme, and a marker of a busy corridor on foot
busstops.notes: One row per route and stop, reduced to distinct stops with the route count kept. A bus stop is a no standing zone as long as a bus, so it clears curb. The dataset describes the network now, so a stop that moved during the study period is recorded only at its present position; that makes the bus stop part of any pre-clearance split weaker than the hydrant part, and the split is therefore reported for hydrants alone as well. in_effect is published as text and not as a boolean, so a query must compare it against a quoted string.

lenient.note: a generous junction box; counts a device that merely reaches the corner

default.note: a junction box of 12 m, about a crosswalk plus a corner radius on an ordinary New York street

strict.note: only a device physically in the crossing area, and only a short bump counts as a corner bump

curb_note: A fire hydrant bans parking within 15 feet under state law and a bus stop is a no standing zone, so a corner carrying either already had cleared curb before this programme reached it. Both layers are current snapshots and carry no installation date, so neither is a treatment and neither can be given an event time.
geometry_note: A polyline is drawn as published and is simplified to at most 12 vertices for display. Two sources publish a segment rather than a device: VZV speed humps have a median geometry length of 217 m and the Speed Reducer Tracking System 81 m, so proximity to one of those lines means the site is on a block carrying a hump and not that a hump is at the corner. Raised crosswalks and turn calming publish true points.
warning: Changing the rule changes which devices count as being at a junction. That is the point of the control: no single rule is correct, and a claim that moves a lot between rules is a claim about the rule.
